posts.author: pavinjoseph
posts.text: Bear Put spread , is it to better to book profit now — Your thesis has come true, but the trade hasn’t paid off as you expected. A bear put spread has some negative theta, so holding it longer would eat away at your premium. To profit more off this trade you need: either a continuation of the move downward hold it to expiry (dangerous as you could take max loss) and have the index stay well below the BEP. Give yourself more time to be right next time - choose monthly or next month expiry. Target 50% of the max profit. Close the trade at the midpoint of the contract duration.

posts.text: Nifty Index Vs Futures contract — This is how I understand it: I think of it simply as Options follow Futures and Futures follow Spot. . When we buy an ATM Call and sell an ATM Put of the same strike and expiry, we are basically creating a synthetic futures/forward position. So, if before expiry the Spot moves up by 400 points but the Futures moves only 200 points, I would expect the synthetic position to be closer to the 200-point futures move , rather than the full 400-point spot move. It may not be exactly 200 because of carry, time to expiry, etc. At expiry, futures and spot converge, so t…

posts.author: TraderJini
posts.text: Anybody tried short strangle in GOLD/SILVER? — Yes, I’ve tried short strangles in Gold/Silver however ended up in losses. They can work well in range-bound markets, but the risk is much higher than indices. Be extra cautious with war/geopolitical news, US data, Fed events, CPI/NFP, or any major unexpected event. Gold and Silver can make very sharp moves during such events, and adjustments can become difficult. I prefer smaller positions, wider strikes, and predefined adjustment/stop-loss rules. Don’t focus only on win rate one big move can wipe out many small profits.

posts.text: Are fno traders are really gamblers "Sattebaaz"? — Gambling doesn’t mean that everyone is there to lose. But the economics of gambling often creates a very uneven outcome. A large proportion of participants eventually lose, while only a small proportion manage to succeed through some combination of expertise, experience, discipline, or sometimes simply luck. Those with larger capital are often economically compelled to stay in the game longer and can afford to “float” through losses and volatility. Those with smaller capital, on the other hand, are often forced by economics to take larger risk…

If the units were bought back before 3:30 PM, the pledged quantity and margin could be restored. However, once the 3:30 PM unpledge process is completed, the original units are released and the system should not restore the old margin against them. posts.author: Ranjit_DailyTrader
posts.text: Are Technical Indicators a Trading Edge or Just Noise? — They can improve trading, but only if you understand what each one is actually telling you. Using too many indicators at the same time can definitely create confusion. For me, Market Profile and Order Flow are more useful for understanding where buyers and sellers are active, while VWAP helps identify the broader intraday bias. RSI can be useful as an additional confirmation, but I wouldn’t use it alone for entries. The key is to have a clear setup and rules. More indicators don’t mean better trades—better interpretation does.

posts.author: Ranjit_DailyTrader
posts.text: What is entry and exit point on Order flow chart — I look for strong buying/selling aggression, absorption, and a clear shift in order flow around important support/resistance levels. I don’t enter just because I see high volume. I prefer to see price accept the level and order flow continue in the same direction rather than entering on the first spike. If the order flow that supported my entry gets completely absorbed or reverses, that’s my signal that the trade idea is invalid. I usually book partial profits at the first major level and trail the remaining position if the order flow continue…

posts.author: Akash_Shah
posts.text: Does GSEC worth for 3 Year Investment than FD? — Historically bond MF were favored because of better tax treatment, now most of that advantage is gone. In higher tax bracket debt MF still has some advantage as you pay tax on FD interest every year, against MF where you pay tax only on redemption, so you can let money compound. Also, MF provides better liquidity compared to FD as you ca take out money any time, without any penalties. And over a longer cycle debt MF will offer slightly better returns than FD. But yeah not a lot of advantage now, as the taxation has changed.

posts.author: KarthikAcharya
posts.text: Deep ITM Options — Hi Amit, Yes, you can place buy/sell orders in deep ITM options. However, if the option is illiquid, your order will execute only if there’s a counterparty available at your price. For illiquid options, a limit order is generally preferable to a market order. If there’s no buyer/seller at your specified price, the order will remain unexecuted. Hence, if it’s a stock option, they are physically settled if they expire ITM, while index options will be cash-settled.

posts.text: Liquidity issue related query — If the strike stays OTM, it will expire worthless and there will be no physical delivery obligation. If it turns ITM and there is no liquidity to exit, it can result in a physical delivery obligation. You can buy the stock on expiry day, which will be netted off against the delivery obligation. Alternatively, buying the corresponding futures position should also work. With CAS, you get an additional 10 minutes after the closing price is determined, so you can assess whether the option has turned ITM and take action accordingly.

posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: Gifting MF units in Zerodha — Yes, if the mutual funds are invested in your daughter’s name from the beginning, no transfer is required when she turns 18 and no tax arises on you or your wife or grandparents. No. A gift of mutual fund units from a parent is tax-exempt in the hands of the daughter; tax arises only when she sells them. The original cost of acquisition and holding period are carried forward; she does not get fresh units at the transfer-day NAV. Her cost will remain ₹10 per unit (your original purchase price), and capital gains will be computed accordingly when she sells them.

posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: Intraday trade on 30/3/2026 (settled 2/4/2026) — trade date or settlement date for tax FY 2025-26 — Trade date is considered for the purpose of reporting in ITR. Since the trade was carried out on the same day it would be considered as Intraday only. Brokers in their report consider settlement date. You can manually adjust that entry and show it as an Intraday.

posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: Tax on debt and fund of funds — Hello @tax007 Capital gains from US Stock or funds of Indian AMC investing in US market would not be treated as debt funds and hence the changes in capital gains for pre and post April 2023 would not be applicable. The taxability depends on the period of holding if the funds have been held for less than 24 months then it would be treated as STCG taxable at slab rates otherwise LTCG taxable at 12.5%. If the gains are STCG taxable at slab rates then benefit of rebate under 87A would be applicable.

posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: FIFO rule transferred shares — It would not be considered as sales because it is just a transfer from demat to another demat. However it would reflect in the profit and loss statement. You can ignore such transaction in the calculations of capital gains.

posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: 7.50% GG 2056 Yield — Hello, G-Sec interest/coupon is taxable as “Income from Other Sources”. If you hold the G-Sec till maturity and receive the face value/principal , the principal repayment itself is generally not taxable. Capital gain may arise if you sell/transfer the G-Sec before maturity at a price different from its cost. Filing ITR-4 under presumptive taxation does not make G-Sec interest tax-free.

posts.author: cvs
posts.text: US 10-Year Yield Crosses 5% — I wouldn’t put it like that, what i was going for is more like - When the broad-market estimates the risk associated with it as requiring 3% returns, (strictly speaking 5% - one’s own switching costs), then being able to lock-in 5% returns from it starts to look attractive. Otherwise, higher returns from it due to its evolving risk profile, doesn’t make it a more attractive instrument, unless one happens to be immune to (already hedged against) those specific risks. An exception being the potential “free lunch” provided by any diversification.

posts.author: KaranAggarwal
posts.text: Which SIP platform would you recommend for long-term investing: Zerodha Coin, Groww, Kuvera, ICICI Direct or another platform? — For a 20–30-year horizon, I would focus less on the app and more on the underlying structure. Choose a platform offering direct mutual funds, clear ownership records, reliable SIP/redemption processes, responsive support, and a straightforward nominee/inheritance process. Also check how it handles NRIs if you move abroad. Zerodha Coin, Groww, Kuvera, ICICI Direct and ET Money can all be evaluated on these parameters rather than UI or popularity alone.

posts.text: New price band and pre-open rules for ETFs from September 7, 2026 — This should improve price discovery and liquidity across ETFs, as the flexible price bands will reduce instances of ETFs getting stuck at the upper or lower circuit despite a genuine move in the underlying. For Gold and Silver ETFs, the pre-open session will also help capture overnight moves in global commodity prices and arrive at a fairer opening price. However, investors should still compare the traded price with iNAV and use limit orders when volumes are low.

posts.text: Level-k thinking - Is there a "correct" depth of reasoning in financial modelling? — On the topic of LLMs, when i find a post or a train of thought i agree with, i find it helpful to prompt an LLM with something like - “List all issues (including logical fallacies) with the following… < the actual text or link to the text >” Helps one overcome one’s blind-spots. Due to the nature of the prompt, there ARE false-positives. However, often it’s easier to identify and ignore the false-positives, than trying to brainstorm potential red-flags.

posts.author: Gagan_suryaputra
posts.text: Need Nifty Small Cap Index F&O contracts for Hedging — I agree with the problem, but I’m not sure a small-cap F&O contract solves it cleanly. If your portfolio is mostly small caps, hedging with Nifty or even Midcap can leave you with a pretty big mismatch. Your stocks could fall sharply while the index barely moves. A small-cap index would give a closer hedge, but liquidity becomes the bigger question. If the underlying stocks themselves aren’t very liquid, the index derivative may end up being thinly traded too. Not sure if there’s enough actual hedging demand first. Otherwise, we could end…

posts.author: ema200wizard
posts.text: Need Nifty Small Cap Index F&O contracts for Hedging — I can understand the demand from a hedging point of view, especially for someone holding a small-cap portfolio. But small-caps are already quite volatile, and adding derivatives could make things even more risky. Plus, the exchange criteria (source) and relatively lower volumes in small-cap stocks could make this difficult to launch and trade smoothly. And honestly, most of us, including me, might end up using it not just for hedging but to make some quick money. After all, who doesn’t like to dip their hands in a little?
